18.32.7.en: 6- David's overwhelming victory over his enemies appears in that they were wasting away, that is, perishing; and even those who fortified themselves in strong fortresses he defeated, so they fled and crept out of their fortresses, and He destroys them also.

18.32.8.en: Satan has no authority over you; rather, by the power of Christ you can overcome him, and he flees from you. So resist him and cast away all his evil methods until you tread them down with your feet, and trust that God will help you however weak you are, and you will regain your place as a child of God whatever your falls.

18.33.0.en: 46- “The Lord liveth; and blessed be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.”

18.33.1.en: 1- After David reviewed God's works with him and how He saved him from his enemies, and even gave him victory over them so that they fled from him or submitted to him, he now offers thanks and praise to God; that is, his experience with God increased, so his love and praise of God increased.

18.33.2.en: 2- David felt that God is living, and feels for His children and supports them in all their afflictions; even if He is long-suffering for a time for a wisdom of His own, He certainly intervenes at the right time and delivers His children. He is unlike the pagan gods, which are stones, unable to help their followers.

18.33.3.en: 3- He offers thanks and blessing to God because He is a rock and an unshakable fortress; everything in the world changes except God alone, with whom “is no variableness, neither shadow of turning” (Jas 1:17).

18.33.4.en: 4- David feels that God, who saved him from his enemies, is exalted beyond measure above the pagan gods and all the powers of the world; He is lofty in His thoughts, His love, His dealings with men and His power. He deserves meditation and praise every day and forever. This verse shows the extent of David's attachment to God.

18.34.0.en: 47- “It is God that avengeth me, and subdueth the people under me.”

18.34.1.en: 1- David thanks the just God, who keeps the righteous and punishes the wicked; as He blessed David and glorified him, so He avenged him on his enemies, such as Saul, Nabal, Absalom and all the nations that rose up against him. How they all perished!

18.34.2.en: 2- God did not only avenge David, but turned the enemies into friends, as they submitted to him, such as Abner the commander of Saul's army, who was reconciled with David, and like the nations that offered gifts and submitted to David.

18.34.3.en: 3- This verse applies to Christ, who avenged Himself on His enemies the demons by binding them with His Cross; as for the Jews who persisted in opposing Him, they perished, and Jerusalem their city was destroyed in AD 70 at the hands of the Romans; and God subdued the nations that opposed Christ, so they became believers and joined the Church.

18.35.0.en: 48- “He delivereth me from mine enemies: yea, thou liftest me up above those that rise up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.”

18.35.1.en: 1- After thanking God the Living One, the Rock and the Support (v. 46), David thanked God who avenges him on his enemies (v. 47), and in this verse he thanks God who delivers him from his enemies.

18.35.2.en: 2- David praises and thanks God because He delivered him from his enemies, such as Saul and the Philistines and Absalom his son. He has repeated the same meaning found in this verse in the previous verses of this Psalm, for he ascribes the glory to God in his victories over his enemies, and not to his own strength or anything else.

18.35.3.en: 3- He thanks God also because He not only delivered him from his enemies but glorified him and lifted him above his enemies, that is, subdued them to him or destroyed them. This is what happens with everyone who trusts in God if he is patient in his striving.

18.35.4.en: 4- This verse applies to Christ also, because the Father lifted Him above His enemies the demons by His death on the Cross and His Resurrection, and the priests, the Pharisees, the scribes and everyone who opposed Christ were put to shame when they faced the power of His Resurrection and the miracles that took place at the hands of the Apostles.

18.36.0.en: 49- “Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name.”

18.36.1.en: 1- For all the works of God that he mentioned in this Psalm, David praises and sings to God; how beautiful it is for a person to remember God's kindnesses to him every day.

18.36.2.en: 2- David was not content with praising God among his people, but also praises Him before the pagan nations, and by this he preaches to them indirectly, for he believes that the expected Messiah will offer salvation to the whole world, Jews and Gentiles. It is a prophecy about the acceptance of the Gentiles into faith in Christ.

18.37.0.en: 50- “He is the tower of salvation for his king; and sheweth mercy to his anointed, to David, and to his seed for evermore.”

18.37.1.en: 1- In conclusion David thanks God, who saved him from his enemies and gives him an opportunity to enjoy the true salvation, which is fellowship with God. David likens this salvation to a tower, that is, a permanent immunity, which King David enjoys. And everyone who reigns over himself, that is, controls his lusts, Christ gives him salvation and lasting joy.

18.37.2.en: 2- In the midst of this joy and praise David does not forget his weakness, so he speaks with humility to God and praises Him for His mercy to him; for he, the one anointed as king, deserves nothing, but all that he has is grace and mercy from God.

18.37.3.en: 3- David concludes the Psalm with great faith that all the preceding blessings God gives to him and to his seed after him, and to everyone of his seed who believed and lived with God and reigned on the throne of the kingdom of Judah, until it reaches Christ, who came from the seed of David and who reigns forever, and indeed makes those who believe in Him, who are of David's faith, reign with Him forever in His Kingdom.

18.37.4.en: Praise is a delight to which no delight in the world compares; it is a pledge of the Kingdom that you can taste from now, so do not deprive yourself of praising God in your private prayer every day, and you will live in joy forever. Nature and the word of God call us to perfection. To the chief musician. A psalm of David. “The heavens declare the glory of God” ... (v. 1) Introduction:

18.37.5.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, as appears in the title of the Psalm.

18.37.7.en: After a quiet sitting or sittings of David in which he contemplated nature, and saw God in it, and enjoyed being in His hands. So he expressed his feelings in this Psalm.

18.37.8.en: 3- This Psalm speaks of three matters:

18.37.9.en: A- God, who created nature and is shown through it if man contemplates it.

18.37.10.en: B- The word of God, which prepares man and leads him to bring him to the Kingdom, and the work of the word of God is manifested in the Incarnation of Christ, to redeem man and to show the way of the Kingdom in Himself, in His saying, “I am the way.”

18.37.11.en: C- Man's response to God as shown in nature and the word of God, in his pursuit of perfection in order to please God.

18.37.12.en: 4- In the title of this Psalm in the Septuagint translation it says “to the end,” and what is meant is the perfection of God's manifestation in nature, and the perfection of the work of His word in man.

18.37.13.en: 5- This Psalm encourages whoever wants to sit in solitude and meditate on God, so it is fitting for a person to repeat it when he is alone with God.

18.37.14.en: 6- This Psalm is found in the prayer of Prime, to lead man at the beginning of his day to look to God and meditate on His creatures and His word.

19.0.0.en: 1- “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.”

19.0.1.en: The firmament: the heavenly bodies and their courses.

19.0.2.en: 1- David began with the heavens, which glorify God, because at the beginning of creation God created heaven first.

19.0.3.en: 2- He mentions the heavens here in the plural, because the Holy Bible mentions to us a number of heavens and not one heaven, as Moses declared (Deut 10:14), and David (Ps 68:33), and Solomon (1 Kgs 8:27), and Nehemiah (Neh 9:6). And Christ Himself, when He taught us to pray, said to us, say, “Our Father which art in heaven” (Mt 6:9) (literally, in the heavens). And the Apostle Paul declared that he was caught up to the third heaven (2 Cor 12:2). So all the heavens glorify God.

19.0.4.en: 3- Nature, that is, the heavens and the firmament, declares the glory of God. How, when it cannot speak? Through its submission to God and the order He has set for it, so they do not collide with one another and carry out His will, and so declare the power of their Creator and His precision through their work, and not through their speech, as the verse mentions.

19.0.5.en: 4- The heavens are the angels and the saints who are in the heavens, for they glorify God and praise Him at all times.

19.0.6.en: 5- The heavens are also the souls of the righteous, who are the Apostles, the Evangelists and the saints everywhere in the world, who praise God, serve Him faithfully, and proclaim His name in their preaching, through their words and works, for their very conduct is itself a glorification of God's name. And the steadfastness of these saints in goodness is like the steadfastness of the heavens and the firmament throughout the ages since God created them.

19.0.7.en: 6- When a person repeats this Psalm and says “The heavens declare the glory of God,” he lifts his eyes upward, and God reveals His works to him and his mind is enlightened, so he understands endless depths of God's love for him.

19.0.8.en: 7- The heavens also symbolize the dwellers of heaven, and the firmament symbolizes the dwellers of earth, that is, the Church triumphant in heaven and the Church militant on earth speak of God and preach Him.

19.0.9.en: 8- When a person looks at the sky and sees all that God has done for his sake, he rejoices greatly, and is humbled before God, who loved him and did all this for him.

19.0.10.en: 9- The heavens symbolize the dwelling of God, so they represent the work of grace, and the firmament means the earth where man dwells, so it represents spiritual striving, and so the work of grace and striving are completed together that man may receive his salvation, and by them God is glorified.

19.0.11.en: 10- This part of the Psalm (vv. 1-6) resembles the eighth Psalm, “O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!”; but this Psalm speaks of nature's glorification of God, while the eighth Psalm speaks of the relationship of the Creator with His creation.

19.0.12.en: 11- From this part we see that God gave us two holy books. The first, the Holy Bible, is the one in our hands and includes the books from Genesis to Revelation. The second book is the nature around us, and the two books speak to us of God that we may love Him and glorify Him, and each of them completes the other and confirms it.

19.0.13.en: 12- Every artist is known by his works, and according to their splendor and greatness he is great; how great, then, is God, when we see the nature He created with a precision and perfection in which no one equals Him.

19.1.0.en: 2- “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.”

19.1.1.en: 1- The day represents the daytime in which the greatness of God appears, and after it comes the night with its quiet, which confirms the greatness of God; their precise succession confirms God's power and His ordering of the universe.

19.1.2.en: 2- The day is an opportunity for work and striving, and the night an opportunity for quiet and prayer and for receiving the work of God's grace more fully, so the day and the night symbolize striving and grace.

19.1.3.en: 3- The day has light and symbolizes the shining saints, who make known the word of God through their lives and words.

19.1.4.en: 4- The night symbolizes obscurity, for man knows of the mysteries of God only what the Holy Spirit reveals to His children who believe in Him, who watch with Him in prayer and praise.

19.1.5.en: 5- The day symbolizes the periods of ease and relief that God gives His children. The night and the darkness symbolize the distress that comes upon God's children, and during both God works and gives His blessings.

19.1.6.en: 6- The day symbolizes the New Testament, where Christ became incarnate and declared great mysteries and salvation for mankind, and the night symbolizes the Old Testament, where there are prophecies and types, which were declared and made manifest in the New Testament.

19.1.7.en: 7- God makes known His knowledge by works visible in the day and in the daytime, that is, He utters speech. And also in the night He shows knowledge, so He declares deep mysteries about Himself to everyone who loves Him and watches with Him, for He always wants His children to know Him and enjoy fellowship with Him.

19.2.0.en: 3- “There is no saying nor speech; their voice is not heard.”

19.2.1.en: 1- The speaking of the sun, the moon, the stars and all the planets, through their submission to the order God has set for them, is stronger than the words of human languages; for any language is understood by some people, or races, or the educated, but the speech of the heavenly bodies can reach every person, and so proclaims the power of God the Almighty.

19.2.2.en: 2- If the great heavenly bodies were to speak with the words of human languages, or with any voice, it would be an annoying voice that men could not bear. But their speaking without a voice conveys the meaning God wants quietly to every person, when he contemplates these heavenly bodies, and so glorifies God.

19.2.3.en: 3- The Church throughout history, by its Apostles, its martyrs and all its servants, has spoken through their lives and conduct with a power that surpasses every human language and every sermon that moves people, because their lives were a practical application of Christ's commandments, and an example that cannot be resisted.

19.3.0.en: 4- “Their speech is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun,”

19.3.1.en: 1- The earth symbolizes the earthly who walk according to the flesh and not according to the Spirit; to these will come the voice of the heavenly bodies, which declare God to them, that they may believe in Him and walk by the Spirit, and so their concern for fleshly things will lessen.

19.3.2.en: 2- The voice of these heavenly bodies will also reach, without a word, every place where any person lives, that is, God will call all mankind by means of these bodies, that they may believe in Him and leave their sins and live to Him.

19.3.3.en: 3- The speech of these heavenly bodies symbolizes the preaching of the Apostles, which reached the end of the world, and Christianity spread in the world when it reached the capital of the Roman Empire, which ruled the world, and from it spread to all the lands.

19.3.4.en: 4- The sun has a dwelling and a resting place among these heavenly bodies, and this symbolizes Christ the Sun of Righteousness, who dwelt in our flesh and walked among creatures as one of us, to redeem us and to be an example to us of pure and perfect conduct.

19.3.5.en: 5- Our Lady the Virgin Mary is the dwelling in which the Sun of Righteousness dwelt, that is, Christ our God was born of her.

19.3.6.en: 6- The Church also is where the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God, dwelt, through His Holy Sacraments and all the work of the Holy Spirit in the believers. And the Church became manifest before the whole world, declaring that she is the house of God in which He dwells.

19.3.7.en: 7- The Sun of Righteousness, our Lord Jesus Christ, dwelt likewise in those who believe in Him, so they became light for the world.

19.4.0.en: 5- “Which is as a bride coming out of her chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race in the way.” The bride: what is meant is the bridegroom, because the Hebrew original of the word means both masculine and feminine, but here we see that the rest of the words of the verse are masculine (such as “coming out,” “rejoiceth”). The chamber: the private room of the bride and bridegroom.

19.4.1.en: 1- He likens the sun to the bridegroom coming out of the marriage chamber (his chamber), by which he means the womb of the Virgin, from which He was born to redeem mankind, or the bosom of the Father, in which He was from eternity, and His bride, the Church, was in His heart before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:4). The Bridegroom came out of His chamber joyful and rejoicing, and moved with power to complete our salvation, like the sun that moves as a strong man going out to the race, and no one can stand in its way.

19.4.2.en: 2- As the sun is strong and its movement cannot be stopped, so Christ completed our salvation with power on the Cross, and the devil with all his wiles and wickedness could not hinder His salvation; on the contrary, when Christ died on the Cross He was in the fullness of strength, for by His death He bound Satan, and he no longer had authority to take those who believe in Christ to Hades.

19.4.3.en: 3- Christ offered us a salvation full of exultation and joy, and at the same time a mighty, powerful salvation that crushes the evil in us and gives us a new life in Him, and by this we receive in Christ lasting joy and the strength to crush Satan, who fights us during our spiritual striving on earth. The might of Christ He gives to us in the strength and continuity of our striving, whatever Satan's hindrances.

19.4.4.en: 4- Christ the Bridegroom, who prepared for us the chamber, that is, the place of the wedding, and we were in His heart before He created us, came in the fullness of time and redeemed us on the Cross, and ascended to heaven, and prepared for us a place, which is the chamber in which we shall enjoy His embrace forever; and out of the abundance of His love for us He lets us enjoy His chamber in part while we are on earth, when He reigns over our hearts and lets us enjoy fellowship with Him, that we may be encouraged until we reach the heavenly chamber.

19.5.0.en: 6- “His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.”

19.5.1.en: 1- The sun symbolizes Christ the Sun of Righteousness, of clear power; from the end of the heavens to the ends of it, and His care for His creatures is clear to all, even if the atheists deny it.

19.5.2.en: 2- The Incarnation of Christ was known in the whole world, and His redemption and His death on the Cross, but many neglected it and some denied it.

19.5.3.en: 3- At the Second Coming of Christ He will appear, and the whole world will know Him from the end of the heavens to the ends of them.

19.5.4.en: 4- God showed His action and power, not only by His light like the sun, but also by the heat of the work of His Holy Spirit, which affects people's feelings, and no one can hide from the work of the Holy Spirit, though he can refuse this work and try to quench this heat. And though a person may be unable to see the light of the sun, like the blind, yet he cannot keep away from the heat of the sun that affects him; God seeks everyone and calls everyone to believe in Him and repent.

19.5.5.en: 5- The heat of the sun symbolizes the warmth of the divine love and mercy that God gives to men, and makes men show compassion to one another and love one another.

19.5.6.en: God calls you by means of all His creatures to love Him and worship Him and enjoy fellowship with Him, so always look at the nature around you and seek God in it, and then He will reveal Himself to you and let you enjoy seeing Him.

19.6.0.en: 7- “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making the ignorant wise.”

19.6.1.en: 1- The sun covers the world with its light and heat, and likewise the word of God lights up a person's life, moves his feelings, cares for him and leads him on the way to God.

19.6.2.en: 2- In this verse and the following verses he explains the work of the word of God in man in six actions, just as the days of creation, which were created by the word of God, are six. And as God rested on the seventh day, so the soul rests in the end by its being with God.

19.6.3.en: 3- The law of the Lord is the Law of Moses and the Ten Commandments, and it is also the law of Christ, that is, the teachings of the New Testament. The law of the Lord is perfect because God is its giver, and it cannot be lacking in anything, and it calls men to perfection and turns souls back from the deviations of sin.

19.6.4.en: 4- God's word is called, in addition to being a law, that is, an order and a statute, a testimony, that is, it testifies before man to the right way to God, and testifies against man if he sins that he deserves punishment, and testifies for the righteous that they held fast to the word of God.

19.6.5.en: 5- Even if all men lie, the word of God remains true and faithful, and there is no falsehood in it. And because it is the word of God it can turn the ignorant from his ignorance to wisdom, so he walks in the way of God, keeps away from sin, and goes on the way to the Kingdom of Heaven.

19.6.6.en: 6- The testimony of the Lord is sure because it testifies to the bitterness of sin and its corruption of man, and at the same time it testifies also to the truth of God's promises and the life-giving effect of His words in souls.

19.7.0.en: 8- “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

19.7.1.en: 1- God's commandments are upright amid the crooked, perverted teachings of the world, which lead to the ways of destruction, but God's upright commandments ensure arrival at God and enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

19.7.2.en: 2- Those who incline to uprightness rejoice in God's upright commandments, because they help them reach God, and also make their will like the will of God, so they rejoice in the knowledge of God and the sweetness of the upright life.

19.7.3.en: 3- Everyone who meditates on God's commandments discovers their uprightness and their loftiness above all the thoughts of the world, and as he walks in them he can see God, and his heart rejoices.

19.7.4.en: 4- If the person who strives on the way to the Kingdom sins, and then looks at God's upright commandments, he finds them a help to him in reaching the way of the Kingdom, so he regains his joy with the tears of repentance.

19.7.5.en: 5- The word of God, that is, His commands, is pure and clean with no purpose but the knowledge of God, so it can purify everyone who holds fast to it, and then his mind and his eyes are enlightened, so he sees God and enjoys fellowship with Him.

19.7.6.en: 6- God's pure commands lift man above the thoughts of men, and God gives him spiritual enlightenment with all the wisdom, discretion and discernment they carry, so he discovers the sweetness of being with God and discerns sin, and so keeps away from all that leads to it.

19.7.7.en: 7- Whoever lives by God's pure commands receives the wisdom with which he can guide others; the servant, and every father and mother and all educators need the word of God, which gives them wisdom, so that they can guide others.

19.7.8.en: 8- God's pure commands are the conscience, that is, the voice of God within man, which enlightens his eyes, so that he sees God in all who are around him and in all creatures.

19.7.9.en: 9- God's pure commands in their perfection are also the work of the Holy Spirit, who enlightens man's eyes and guides him in all his ways, and no one can twist the words of the Holy Spirit, as sometimes happens with the conscience.

19.8.0.en: 9- “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.”

19.8.1.en: 1- The word of God plants the fear of God in the heart, so it keeps away from every sin and man is established forever, where he enjoys fellowship with God in the Kingdom.

19.8.2.en: 2- The fear of God purifies man's heart from sin, so that he can see God, and by this he abides in God forever.

19.8.3.en: 3- The fear of God purifies man's heart, so he sees everything as clean and sees God in it, so he lives with God and endures in Him forever, because he passes over sin and rejects it.

19.8.4.en: 4- The word of God is His judgments, which judge everything in the world; it is the measure of what is right and exposes errors, so however crooked men's measures become, the word of God remains the sound truth declared to men.

19.8.5.en: 5- The word of God is altogether righteous; it cannot show partiality to one person against another, whatever his circumstances, and it leads all to the salvation of their souls, and it is also the source of justice for everyone who seeks it; so to the extent that the laws and statutes of men submit to the word of God they become just laws.

19.9.0.en: 10- “More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.”

19.9.2.en: The honeycomb (drippings): pure bees' honey, free of wax.

19.9.3.en: 1- He describes the word of God as more to be desired and better than all the possessions of the world and the most precious of them, like pure gold; the word of God is the pearl of great price, for which the merchant sells all the pearls to acquire it.

19.9.4.en: 2- Likewise the word of God has a spiritual delight that surpasses all sensual delights, for it is sweeter than honey and the honey drained of wax.

19.9.5.en: 3- If sins and evil lusts have their pleasures, they are all corrupt; but the word of God is pure honey, indeed sweeter than it, because it is a delight refined of everything, by which man knows God and enjoys fellowship with Him.

19.10.0.en: 11- “Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.”

19.10.1.en: 1- God's commandments and His law warn David of sins, and by this he knows wrong things and keeps away from them, so he lives the upright life and does not turn aside from the truth. That is, God's commandment protects him from sin and leads him on the way to the Kingdom.

19.10.2.en: 2- David's obedience and love for the commandment appear in his holding fast to it and keeping it. What is meant by keeping it is applying it in his life, and not only keeping it in the mind, that is, that he lives by it and tastes its sweetness, so he enjoys fellowship with God through it.

19.10.3.en: 3- Also when David keeps God's word he receives the eternal reward and the great recompense, that is, the happy eternal life.

19.10.4.en: Be careful to read the Holy Bible and meditate on it every day, so that you can apply it in your life, and you will touch God's work and His blessing on all your works, and also on your words and thoughts, and you will feel the delight of divine fellowship.

19.11.0.en: 12- “Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.”

19.11.1.en: Errors (oversights): the sins to which a person does not pay attention, that is, they escape him and he does not notice them, either because of their smallness, or because it is not clear that they are sin.

19.11.2.en: 1- David the prophet declares his weakness before God, and that he is unable to discover the sins of oversight, and asks for God's forgiveness and tolerance toward him for these sins; however much he keeps God's word he will overlook some sins, because God in His perfection charges His angels with folly (Job 4:18), how much more man's weakness and his falling into many lapses.

19.11.3.en: 2- In the press of life, though a person knows the sins, he overlooks them and falls into them. And Satan may depict justifications for them to him, so that he feels they are not sin, and this is from man's weakness, but the merciful God forgives him if he is striving on the way of repentance.

19.11.4.en: 3- Because of the weakness of his understanding, though he keeps the commandment, a person may not understand that some things are wrong, that is, in his practical application he falls into some sins without feeling it, and needs divine guidance and also forgiveness from God.

19.11.5.en: 4- A person meets many things in his life that distract his mind, and during this distraction Satan slips in sins, so he needs divine warning.

19.11.6.en: 5- Secret sins are sins hidden from the person himself, that is, he does not know that they are sin, so he needs guidance and clarification from God, and this is what happens when there is much reading in the Holy Bible and spiritual books: a person discovers every day some of these secret sins.

19.11.7.en: 6- Secret sins may be hidden from people but known to the person himself, such as sins of thought and of the heart, and David asks God to forgive him for them; he offers repentance between himself and God, even if people do not see his sins.

19.12.0.en: 13- “Keep back thy servant also from the proud; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.”

19.12.1.en: 1- By “the proud” he means their sin, that is, pride, and so he asks God to keep him from it, and in the Hebrew original it says, “and also from the sins done in pride”; it is a continuation of the previous verse, that is, the oversights and the secret sins, and he adds the sin of pride, especially since what is done in pride a person may persist in and justify, so that it is hard to offer repentance for it.

19.12.2.en: 2- David asks God with humility that if he falls into a sin in pride he may repent of it, and he calls on God not to let this sin have dominion over him; David's distinction is his haste to repent and his fear of sin, which makes him keep away from it.

19.12.3.en: 3- David also hopes that he will not be a cause of another's falling into the sin of pride, or what is connected with it, such as judging, which was when he fell into the sin of adultery with the wife of Uriah the Hittite and exposed Uriah to be killed in the war; so he fears that he caused his people to stumble and made them fall into judging and pride.

19.12.4.en: 4- Because of the seriousness of the sin of pride David feels that by being rid of it and all that follows it he walks in the way of perfection, because the sin of pride is the mother of many sins, such as anger, hatred and murder, so by being cleansed from the great sin of pride he is rid of many sins. He does not concentrate on the sin of adultery and murder despite their seriousness, but the more serious are the mother sins, such as pride.

19.12.5.en: When you examine yourself, be concerned to discover the cause of your sins, that is, the mother sin that made you fall into these sins, so examine the extent of your selfishness or your pride, to treat it, and you will be rid of the sins that result from it.

19.13.0.en: 14- “Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my rock, and my redeemer.”

19.13.1.en: 1- At the close of the Psalm, after David showed his great care concerning the mother sins such as pride, he asks God that his words and thoughts may be according to God's will, that is, that what shows outwardly in him and what is within him may please God.

19.13.2.en: 2- By the words of the mouth he means not only that in dealing with others he keeps God's commandments and law, but also that his prayers, that is, his speaking with God, be in the fitting manner that pleases God, that is, with humility, love and submission to Him.

19.13.3.en: 3- If a person's thoughts and the intentions of his heart are pleasing to God, his words also become pure, for out of the abundance of the heart the tongue speaks, and finally his actions are upright.

19.13.4.en: 4- The words of the mouth and the meditation of the heart include words, thoughts and inner feelings, and all of these are expressions of the prayer that man offers to God, whether by the tongue, or by thought, or by feelings, as St. John Climacus says, “Let your tongue be silent so that your heart may speak.”

19.13.5.en: 5- In humility David thanks God, who is the cause of the purity of his words, thoughts and feelings, for he says to Him, “You are my rock,” that is, the cause of my strength, my peace and my steadfastness in living with You.

19.13.6.en: 6- In the end David is assured that God is his redeemer, that is, his savior from sins, his defender, and the one responsible for his care, that he may live in purity all the days of his life.

19.13.7.en: God the Savior in distress. To the chief musician. A psalm of David. “The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble” ... (v. 1) Introduction:

19.13.8.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, as we see in the title.

19.13.10.en: David the prophet wrote it before his war with the children of Ammon, whom the great army of Aram supported, and this army had many horses and chariots (2 Sam 10:6, 8; 1 Chr 19:7), and David triumphed by the power of God in this war.

19.13.12.en: When the kings of Judah went out to fight their enemies, or when their enemies attacked them, such as Sennacherib when he besieged Jerusalem, so this Psalm was said to King Hezekiah, that he might trust in the power of God who gives him victory (2 Chr 32). The people used to say this Psalm to the king when he offered sacrifices before God before going out to war (v. 3).

19.13.13.en: 4- This Psalm is a prophecy about Christ, who went forth and triumphed over Satan, not only in the temptation on the mountain, but rather on the Cross, when He bound him by His death for us.

19.13.14.en: 5- It is fitting for the Church, and every believer, to repeat this Psalm in the war with Satan, to trust and establish faith in God, who gives victory over Satan in all spiritual wars.

19.13.15.en: 6- This Psalm can be said at the beginning of the new year to God, who reigns over the hearts of His children and triumphs over the demons and drives them out.

19.13.16.en: 7- This Psalm is connected with the Psalm that follows it, that is, (Ps 21). The twentieth Psalm speaks to us of the king going out to war to triumph over his enemies, while the twenty-first Psalm is a prayer of thanksgiving after the victory over the enemies.

19.13.17.en: 8- This Psalm shows the importance of prayer for others, especially the leader, that is, the king, and every person responsible in his place, because of the seriousness of the leader's position, and at the same time it shows his need for the prayer of those who follow him.

19.13.18.en: 9- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya at the beginning of the prayer of the Third Hour, in which appears the work of the Holy Spirit, who supports man in his spiritual war.
